name: Panel
purpose: The shared bordered, rounded content container that nearly every other component is built from.
useWhen: Grouping related content that needs a visible boundary from the surrounding page.
avoidWhen: A lighter separation (spacing alone, a rule) would do — not every group of content needs a panel.
anatomy: Surface modifier (pale / tint / ice / dark / blue)
Content wrapper (.isq-content — see Foundations > Widths for the density modifiers it accepts)
responsive: Panel padding reduces at narrow widths via the .isq-content density modifiers it wraps; no structural change.
accessibility: No semantic meaning of its own — the content inside carries structure (headings, lists).
html: Panel content.

name: Button
purpose: Primary, secondary and light calls to action.
useWhen: A single clear action per area — one primary action, optionally one secondary.
avoidWhen: Never use vague labels such as “Click here” — label the destination or outcome.
responsive: Full-width on narrow screens where it is the primary action in a stacked layout.
accessibility: Use a real <button> or <a>, never a styled <div>.
Visible focus ring at sufficient contrast.
External links state their destination behaviour via aria-label.
html: Open resource↗

name: Callout
purpose: Default, blue, success, warning and error messages that need to stand apart from body text.
useWhen: A short reinforcing message, a state result, or a boundary note within a panel.
avoidWhen: Multiple callouts in succession — choose the one point that deserves emphasis.
responsive: Stacks naturally; no restructuring at narrow widths.
accessibility: Colour is always paired with the message text itself — never a colour-only cue.
Use role="status" for callouts injected dynamically after an interaction.
knownLimitations: --isq-warning uses the same value as body charcoal rather than a distinct hue — confirm this is intentional (see Decisions).
html: This raises Sarah’s concern further. Sarah reviews section 10 of the Child Protection Act 1999.

name: Meta tags
purpose: Compact duration, category or format labels.
useWhen: Metadata needs to be scannable at a glance beside a title.
avoidWhen: The value is essential instruction — metadata is a label, not the content itself.
responsive: Wraps to a new line rather than truncating.
accessibility: Plain text — no icon-only meta items without a text label.
html: 40 min Compliance

name: Card grid
purpose: Two- or three-column card collection.
useWhen: Comparing three or more parallel options with consistent criteria.
avoidWhen: Fewer than three items — a split or standard panel is simpler.
responsive: Restacks to a single column at the 760px breakpoint without removing content.
accessibility: Card title is the link where the card is interactive, so the accessible name stays meaningful.
knownLimitations: "Grid" is named as a layout primitive in Document 2's prose but was missing from its technical class index — corrected here.
html:
Title
Body text.

name: Accordion
purpose: Progressive disclosure of secondary detail that benefits from being collapsed by default.
useWhen: Secondary detail the learner may want but doesn't need to see immediately — e.g. individual pieces of legislation within a set.
avoidWhen: Core obligations the learner must see immediately — never hide essential compliance information behind an interaction.
responsive: Padding and alignment reduce on mobile; touch target remains adequate.
accessibility: Uses native <details>/<summary> so semantics and keyboard behaviour are preserved without JavaScript.
Chevron is aria-hidden; state is exposed natively via the open attribute.
dependencies: Production CSS only — no JavaScript required; native <details> provides the interaction.
html:
Education (Accreditation of Non-State Schools) Act 2017 and Regulation +

Requires schools to maintain and actively implement written child protection processes…

name: Tabs
purpose: Local navigation across a small number of parallel categories.
useWhen: Categories are genuine peers, not sequential steps.
avoidWhen: Sequential steps, or labels too long to remain readable on mobile.
responsive: Left-navigation tabs move above the panel on mobile and may become a horizontally scrollable row.
accessibility: Real buttons for tab triggers, arrow-key navigation between tabs, one visible tabpanel at a time.
dependencies: Requires scoped JavaScript for tab switching (see Harm tabs for the current course-specific implementation).
knownLimitations: The only current implementation of the tabs pattern in the shared CSS is the Harm tabs course-specific variant — a generalised Tabs component has not yet been extracted from it.
html: <!-- See Harm tabs for the current working implementation of this pattern -->

name: Video frame
purpose: Responsive 16:9 embedded media treatment.
useWhen: Video is the best medium for the content — movement, demonstration or human presence adds value text cannot.
avoidWhen: Decorative use, or content a still image and text could communicate as well.
responsive: Maintains 16:9 at any width via aspect-ratio and object-fit, never fixed width/height.
accessibility: Accurate synchronised captions required.
Transcript provided where it supports access, search, review or reuse.

name: Section opener
purpose: Introduces a major course section with strong orientation.
useWhen: Once per genuine major section reset.
avoidWhen: Every subtopic or minor heading change.
responsive: Type scale reduces fluidly; no text clipping or manual line breaks.
accessibility: Correct heading level for a genuine structural transition (usually h2).

name: Dark / footer band
purpose: Closes or resets a section with concise reinforcement.
useWhen: End of a major section, as a deliberate structural close.
avoidWhen: As a general-purpose dark panel unrelated to closing a section.
responsive: Two columns become one; the title remains before the explanatory copy.
accessibility: Sufficient contrast for reversed (light-on-dark) text; verified against the dark surface tokens.
html: Three to five concise points recapping the section.

name: Split card
purpose: Pairs a concise explanation with meaningful imagery.
useWhen: Explanation genuinely benefits from a relevant photograph.
avoidWhen: Generic stock imagery, or content too long to sit comfortably beside media — use a text-led panel instead.
responsive: Restacks to one column at 760px; image uses a fixed aspect ratio.
accessibility: Meaningful alt text on the image; decorative images marked accordingly.
html: Later that afternoon, Karen receives a message from Lily’s mother requesting a meeting.

name: Key message
purpose: Isolates one point a learner should retain.
useWhen: One legal threshold, definition or critical reminder — one to three sentences.
avoidWhen: Routine supporting detail, or several messages stacked in one panel.
responsive: No structural change; stacks naturally.
accessibility: Not colour-dependent — the rule is a secondary visual cue, the text carries the meaning.
html: A parent must be both able and willing to protect the child.

name: Legislation panel
purpose: Separates the legal source from its plain-English meaning.
useWhen: A specific Act, regulation or section underpins a requirement.
avoidWhen: General policy statements with no legislative source — use a standard content panel.
responsive: Restacks to one column; document image scales down rather than disappearing.
accessibility: Instrument name is a real heading; the citation year and jurisdiction are in text, not only the image.
html:
Child Protection Act 1999 (CPA)

The primary function of the CPA is to authorise Child Safety Services to investigate and take action to act protectively for children.

name: Resource card
purpose: Explains a resource and provides a clear action to open it.
useWhen: A supplementary document or external guidance that needs context before the click.
avoidWhen: Essential learning is available only through the external link — bring it into the course.
responsive: Image and content restack to one column at narrow widths.
accessibility: Descriptive aria-label on the action stating destination and that it opens in a new tab.
External-link icon is aria-hidden with a text label carrying the meaning.
html:
Resource

name: Process block
purpose: Shows a genuinely ordered procedure.
useWhen: Order is real and matters to the outcome.
avoidWhen: The steps aren't truly sequential — numbering implies an order that doesn't exist.
responsive: Stacks vertically; step numbers remain aligned with their titles.
accessibility: Marked up as an ordered list where the sequence is meaningful to assistive technology, not only visually numbered.
knownLimitations: "Process" is named as a component in Document 2's prose catalogue but was missing from its technical class index — corrected here.
html:
1. Notice Recognise a possible indicator of harm.
  2. Record Document what was observed or disclosed.

name: Scenario stage
purpose: Presents context, evidence or an update within a running scenario, from the decision-maker's perspective.
useWhen: A discrete stage of a scenario — orient, notice, decide, explain or continue.
avoidWhen: General explanation unrelated to the running scenario.
responsive: Narrative and image restack; the quote remains adjacent to its narrative context.
accessibility: Quoted dialogue uses <blockquote> or clearly marked quotation, not styling alone.

Recognise & respond

“Mum’s boyfriend gets angry… I don’t feel safe when he’s around.”

name: Decision point
purpose: Requires a realistic professional judgement and reveals the reasoning behind the correct response.
useWhen: A genuine professional juncture with credible distractors.
avoidWhen: An obvious answer with implausible distractors — use a native knowledge check for simple recall.
responsive: Options stack full-width; touch targets remain adequate.
accessibility: Real radio inputs, not click handlers on generic elements.
Selected / correct / incorrect states use text and icon, not colour alone.
Feedback is announced and placed immediately after the action that revealed it.
Reset only included where repeating the activity has real learning value.
dependencies: Scoped JavaScript for state management; must support multiple instances on one lesson without shared state.
html:
Decision point

What must Principal Sarah do next?

Select the most appropriate immediate response.

name: Role split
purpose: Clarifies two related audiences, responsibilities or positions by holding them side by side.
useWhen: Comparing two roles or responses where the differences matter to the decision.
avoidWhen: More than two items — use a card grid or table.
responsive: Restacks to one column; both items remain in the same reading order as desktop.
accessibility: Each side is a labelled region so a screen-reader user can tell which role they are reading.
knownLimitations: Document 1's own component audit flags this class as “Approved pattern — confirm naming”; this catalogue entry settles on Role split as the canonical name, matching the CSS class.
The live Child Protection course does not currently use this shared class for its Able/Willing comparison — see the Able/Willing entry in Governance → Audit findings.
html:
Able

Has the capacity to protect the child.

Willing

Shows intent and motivation to protect the child.

name: Self-assessment
purpose: A structured confidence or knowledge self-rating table — the learner rates each statement against a shared scale (e.g. Not at all confident → Very confident).
useWhen: A short set of statements benefits from a consistent, comparable rating scale, typically at the close of a section as a reflective checkpoint.
avoidWhen: A single reflective prompt — use the native reflection block instead.
As a graded or assessed instrument — this component is explicitly framed as having no right or wrong answers.
anatomy: Column headers naming each scale point
Numbered rows, each pairing a statement with radio options across the scale (.isq-self-assessment__row / __table)
responsive: The scale table is the component most at risk on narrow screens — columns of radio buttons do not fit a 375px viewport without horizontal scrolling or restructuring. Recommend a per-row accordion or stacked-scale layout on mobile (see Known limitations); this has not yet been confirmed against the published output.
accessibility: Each row must be a fieldset with a legend naming the statement; each scale point must be a real radio input with a visible, associated text label — never an unlabelled circle.
The numbered badge (1, 2…) is decorative and must not be the only way the statement is identified to assistive technology.
“Save my reflection” must confirm the save state to the user (e.g. a status region), and “Reset” must not silently clear a response without confirmation given there is explicit save action.
dependencies: Scoped JavaScript to manage save/reset state; must support multiple instances per lesson.
owner: Design and development steward — spec drafted from CSS and screenshot; pending sign-off
knownLimitations: This component ships in the production CSS (14 classes) and in the live Child Protection course but appears in none of the six source documents. This entry is a first specification drafted from the class names, the supplied screenshot and standard accessible-rating-table practice — it has not been verified against the actual rendered markup or tested for keyboard/mobile behaviour, and should be confirmed against a real exported course before its status is upgraded from Course-specific.
html:
Self-reflection

How confident do you feel?

Rate your current confidence in each area. There are no right or wrong answers.

Confidence self-rating
Not at all confident Somewhat confident Confident Very confident
1 Understanding your personal reporting obligations

name: Harm tabs
purpose: Specialised content navigation for categories of harm — lets the learner move between related but distinct categories (physical abuse, psychological/emotional abuse, neglect, sexual abuse or exploitation, grooming) without a full page per category.
useWhen: Built specifically for the Child Protection course's five harm categories.
avoidWhen: Do not reuse elsewhere without review — assess for generalisation into the shared Tabs component first.
responsive: Navigation moves above the panel and may become a horizontally scrollable row if labels remain readable.
accessibility: Real buttons for tab triggers, one visible panel, arrow-key navigation expected.
knownLimitations: Document 1's own component audit already flags this as an “assess for generalisation” candidate — it is the working reference for what the generic Tabs component should become.
html:
Physical abuse

Physical abuse may be indicated by injuries, behavioural changes, fear responses or patterns that are not easily explained.

name: Course feedback form
purpose: Structured feedback form treatment for end-of-course response collection.
useWhen: Use only in an agreed pilot — specification may still change.
avoidWhen: Production use outside an agreed pilot until it reaches Approved status.
responsive: Not yet verified at narrow widths — part of why this remains Experimental.
accessibility: Star rating needs an equivalent text/number alternative, not a visual-only control.
Character counter must be associated with the textarea and announced without being disruptive.
dependencies: Scoped JavaScript; a data-handling and storage decision (not yet documented) before wider use.
knownLimitations: Confirm data handling and implementation status before any course beyond the current pilot adopts this.
html: How was this course?

name: Divider
purpose: Transitions between adjoining structural surfaces with an angled decorative edge.
useWhen: Rare and purposeful surface transitions only.
avoidWhen: As a routine section separator — spacing and headings do that job more accessibly.
responsive: Purely decorative — no content to preserve, but the angle should not obscure adjacent text at narrow widths.
accessibility: Purely decorative — must be aria-hidden.
knownLimitations: Document 1's own component audit calls this “Experimental / decorative — review actual use and reduce if necessary”; Document 2 separately labelled it “Restricted”, a status outside the confirmed seven-value lifecycle — folded into Experimental here. Six directional variants for a component flagged for reduction is itself worth reviewing.

name: Editorial reflection
purpose: Large legacy reflection treatment.
useWhen: Existing courses only, for backwards compatibility.
avoidWhen: Any new work — use the native reflection block, a compact approved panel, or Self-assessment where a rating table is genuinely needed.
responsive: Not actively maintained.
accessibility: Not actively maintained — do not treat as a verified accessible baseline.
knownLimitations: Deprecate for new work per Document 1's own component audit; no replacement migration has been scheduled yet.
html: <!-- Legacy — retained for existing courses only; do not use in new work -->
